prompt: There is a bug report in ISSUE.md. Fix the code in this folder so the issue is resolved. Do not ask questions; make the fix.
final_response:
Fixed. The bug was in `cache.py`:

1. **`get` never refreshed recency** — it just looked up the value, so `get(a)` didn't mark `a` as most recently used.
2. **`put` always appended to `order`**, even for an existing key — so updates duplicated keys in the order list and incorrectly counted against capacity.

The fix makes `get` move an accessed key to the end of the recency order, and makes `put` remove an existing key from the order before re-appending it (so updates refresh recency without consuming extra capacity). Eviction still removes the least-recently-used key from the front.

The reported scenario now behaves correctly: `put(a)`, `put(b)`, `get(a)`, `put(c)` evicts `b`, not `a`.
